summary.verdict: ENRICHMENT GENERALIZES (weaker) — the BINARY FBA-essentiality validation holds in a SECOND organism: in M. tuberculosis, FBA-predicted essential genes are enriched for EXPERIMENTAL (DeJesus 2017 Tn-seq) essentiality at odds ratio 7.9 (Fisher p=2.2e-07), precision 68%. So MET1-3's mechanism signal is validated against experiment in BOTH E. coli (PEC, OR 64) AND Mtb (DeJesus, OR 7.9) — not an E. coli quirk. **HONEST BOUNDS (falsify-first): (1) it is MARKEDLY WEAKER than E. coli (OR 7.9 vs 64; recall 9% vs 22%) — the de-novo default-medium CarveMe Mtb GEM is lower-quality than E. coli's iML1515-grade model and DeJesus is a different (in-vitro) medium, so many experimental essentials are missed. (2) The CONTINUOUS growth-ratio AUROC is 0.54 = ESSENTIALLY CHANCE — the fine RANKING does NOT generalize to Mtb, only the binary enrichment does (consistent with MET3, where Mtb's top-k gain was a whisper). (3) Essentiality only, not drug-target/clinical.** Net: the mechanism signal is real in Mtb too, but as a weak binary enrichment, not a strong ranker — the honest two-organism picture.
